reviews.reviewbody: My search through these recordings has failed to uncover one that sounds good enough to listen to much of the show and tell whether it's good or not. If you think it's worth it, some method of balancing the volumes of the different instruments/mics seems necessary for quality purposes.

That other person that was talking about a fruitless search must either be a moron or an axxhole or both. I was at this show & as most shows at the Omni, the boys brought their A game!! Now previous to this show my brother & I had tix to the Dead at Oakland Coliseum for all 3 Chinese New Year shows. And after driving all the way across the country to California we woke up to find that someone had broken into the car & stolen everything including our tix. And then it took us over a week to get home for lack of bread! And after ALL OF THAT & we get to the  Omni & during the 2nd set we get to hear them play "LONG, LONG WAY TO GO HOME" for the first time! It may have been the second time they played it BUT IT WAS THE FIRST TIME WE HEARD IT!! It was almost as if it was written about our own personal experience!!! Because it really was a Long, long, long long way...to go home!!!! But that was over & we were having a good time. Granted, if you try to compare this with 77 it's not easy to give it a bunch of stars but IN MY BOOK, MY FAVORITE DEAD SHOW WAS ALWAYS EITHER THE ONE I WAS AT OR THE NEXT ONE! Until we lost Jerry that is. Although I did see the boys play many times after Jerry passed, it wasn't even close to the same without the man! I never saw any of those 77 shows. My first show was in 88 but I never regretted attending a single concert that he played. Jerry even on his worst night was still better than not seeing him. Cuz you can bet your ass he was trying to make it the best that he could cuz he was that kind of person!!! Lots of love to you Jerry Garcia!!! Its been almost 25 years since we lost you & you are still loved and missed very much!!! And just for that I'm calling this a 5 star show!
Have a nice day 😊

reviews.reviewbody:
At the time, I found this show very disappointing. Help> Slip> Frank's was missing the "umph" I desired that hat trick to deliver. Same Thing was cool, and the first set waddled along. My primary problem was having been spoiled with the Warlocks 10/9/89 show, a tough bit to outshine. Jerry's show the previous November had also set the bar high.

Naturally, the Eyes opener to the second set ignited 3/29/90-ish hopes, but one cannot turn back the clock. Long Way was a bit of a shock to the system. It felt as though Vince was sneering at both his critics and fans. That was an unusual feeling at a Dead show, to be honest. Ouch. From Estimated on, the show improves. Being from Maine, the Drums was special with the featured loons. The Space-> Wheel is rather tasty, and my first So Many Roads sent shivers down me spine.

Hindsight suggests that I should have been more appreciative at the time. Expectations can be that way: we miss the special treats by wanting the gargantuan explosions of a grande finale. Looking back, I can forgive myself. It was tough to top the 87 through 91 run. 

Hampton still rules, though, no matter what.

As always, Miller's mastering slays.

reviews.reviewbody: I sang a little while and then flew on.

Loved this show, my opinion is influenced by the fact I was there , and this SBD sounds great! This was Jerry's last show at "the Mothership". That thought crossed my mind during "last time'' . The usual bugs in the first set were chalked up as the result of "the Michelangelo Virus'' by Bob  during the crowd banter. It was not the most bombastic night but it was enjoyable , and Bruce as always laid it all out there in what was a hometown show for him !

reviews.reviewbody: Excellent show! Fades off a bit after drums, but not much.

In "touch" jerry sez "Say your piece and PISS oFF"  i had to go back and listen twice to verify.

At the time, show seemed rather avg.  I was blown away by rfk 90 and 93, my 1st, 4th and 5th shows.  But for some reason this one didnt grab me.  Maybe lucy didnt hold my hand tight enough or whatever.

I remember in the mezzanine between sets, people were excited about how many songs they played set 1.  Caps Center was a good venue thet seemed to enjoy.

I dunno, im not gonna do my usual intense review of this show unless upon listening to it, i hear something really interesting, in which case i will edit/re-post this review.

Honestly, my friend and i listened to EVERY 92 show last year and took notes and until you get to december when things musically acheive AN ENYIRELY NEW LEVEL OF AWESOMENESS, the only 5 star show in 92 is Charlotte from June.  That show is like, woah, they just clicked x faxtor style.

reviews.reviewtitle: Band on fire to bid Bruce farewell
reviews.reviewbody: First night in the beautiful Palace, considered the NBA's first "luxury arena."  Do I remember velvet curtains?  Had never seen that in a basketball arena before.  And this two night stand was Hornsby's last as a regular member. They definitely were in the mood to send him off properly.  The first set song selection all fits the theme of a farewell party, and they were SMOKIN', every song.  Candace seemed to have can lights in the ceiling rafters creating running and dancing skeletons in the sky, all in unison; it was the wildest light show I've ever seen.  Whole show is great but this is the hottest first set I ever saw.  And the Dew is monumental. First Gloria since '85 so you know the band thought it was special as well.  Thanks Charlie for this updated version!

reviews.reviewbody:
Don’t listen to a lot of Dead post Brent, but this show popped up and I am not disappointed. Charlie Miller always puts out the goods and the show itself is fun with great Jerry ballads to boot. His voice sounds really healthy at this point in time. 
Thanks again Charlie!!

reviews.reviewbody:
It’s been interesting to read up on the various reviews and attendee accounts of this show across archive.org, dead.net, and jerrygarcia.com. Some people’s first show of many, some people’s last show of many. Some folks were bored and disappointed, others dosed and mindblown. Some tuned up by security guards, others treated to a nice, chill time with the boys of summer.

Let me ask you a question about 1990’s Grateful Dead. What’s the difference between 10/1/94 and 10/3/94? Why is one show a legendary triumph, and one just another frog in the pond? The setlist. That’s just about all. The overall performance quality is outstanding in both of those shows. The more I listen, the more willing I am to give any show a fair shot, even when the setlist doesn’t remind me of Pembroke Pines ‘77.

6/14/92 isn’t stacked with a Help > Slip > Frank, Scarlet > Fire, or Dark Star, but that’s very much by design. Why play it safe with the hits when you can stick ‘em with a Candyman or Jack-A-Roe out of the blue? I enjoy a good roll of the dice when it comes to song selection. This is a mature setlist that has both Jerry and Bob omitting the fan favorites in favor of those crafty tunes that hide one or two layers back in the catalog. Desolation Row. Samson. Ship of Fools. Blues numbers. New stuff. Then, they reward the patient with a badass 60’s pairing in the form of The Other One > Morning Dew, and wrap it all up with a trippy Baba O’Riley > Tomorrow Nevers Knows encore. Around 1992, the band members themselves were worried about things getting stale. Rolling into night 1 at Giants Stadium, what better way to shake that notion than with a show like this, one that can appeal to both the jaded touring core and the young NYC heads hitting their first show? Many believe that it’s not just what they play; it’s also how they play it. This is a very focused, proficient performance. The Steve Miller contributions are just gravy.

Jerry’s simple, yet gorgeous guitar solo in Desolation Row at the 4:40 mark tells you everything you need to know about 6/14/92; the groove the boys were in, their total immersion in the music, and the sincerity with which they dished it out to the circus packed in that night out in Jersey.

I like this one a lot. Summer ‘92 had some real goodies, and 6/14/92 is one of them.

reviews.reviewbody: One of a handful of shows sometimes touted as the best of '92 - chiefly due to the first set and having Steve Miller guesting (he opened on this tour). He and the Dead were long-acquainted, having crossed circles for years as Bay Area musicians, since '66. I have this show on tape but probably only listened once, tending to stick to December, and needing to give this tour its due. Though this and the previous night were skipped over by the official Giants Stadium box, putting it in perspective it's a top five show for the year. First Set. Hellina is indeed a powerhouse start, as others have noted. Sugaree is good - not landmark or anything, but good. This is post-Hornsby, but Vince plays a Bruce-like piano riff. This is a perfected Same Thing, settling into the stadium like liquid Play-Doh, filling every row and stairwell. Vince is great, with his Voce DMI emulator. There's a 'We Want Phil' after, but it's gonna be Tennessee. Bobby thinks he's colder than a holy bastard up here, and the song takes that position in the set. Better is Masterpiece. Note the slightly different approach from Jer. Though the set is short, Bird Song is one of the longest ever, @ over 14min, and a must-hear-once, with a couple great sections. Second Set. The We-Want-Phil is answered, though Box is an odd set-opener. But, surprise, it's a solid one. The same goes for Saint. A Sailor probably would have been better than this So Many Roads - but I guess it's a decent-enough version. During the jam for Terrapin Jer switches through several different mods. Drums has a Revenge of the Nerds jam, plus presets beats while Billy and Mickey step out front with their wearable air horns (it's otherwise OK...). Miller comes out for Miracle (it's a Millicle!). During the change-up, Jer taps him and warns him that the key is modulating to G. Then they give him a solo. It's also a 3-guitar lineup for Standing. Miller finds a couple licks after the [shaky] verses, but is unprepared when Jer pauses for the first solo slot. Who wouldn't be, standing next to Jer while he's on the moon? Sheesh. When Bobby enters the verses for Throwing Stones Jer explains the song to Steve. Bobby mostly casually talks his way through, with emphatic punctuations. It doesn't NOT work, but a simpler three-chorder is going to be something they can all bite into. The entry to Not Fade is abrupt, the results great. A unique one. The encore is one of the best examples of a Vince Knockin' (and they were good sports to have Miller come back out). 1st Set:  B 2nd Set: B- Overall = 3¾ stars Highlights: Hell in a Bucket - powerhouse start The Same Thing - settles into corners Not Fade Away - Miller adds to stadium celebration Knockin' on Heaven's Door - presentation of a Vince Knockin' SOURCES: Best-qual SBD is the miller_32449. Best AUD is the schoeps_eD_9972 (n. b. it has a repeated section in Same Thing). The show is usually up on YouTube - sans encore.

reviews.reviewbody: pretty average show until after space/after space everybody lost it casey jones you know!first set alot like the year before didn`t want that but hey after space makes up for everything!

My favorite parts of this show were the ethereal spacy moments. At some point I got tired of all the nonsense up close so I retreated to the absolute rear of RFK as high I could possibly get. From that distance the stage looked like a neon jukebox playing the most beautiful noises. 

There's a shuffling grinding funky improv as the boys pave the way for drums. And space was one of the trippiest ever. Dreamy and hypno with weir and Lesh making what sounded like whale songs while Jerry let out these piercing blasts that sounded like marimba/angels going over a waterfall. The man loved his MIDI.

Later you can hear them toying with a few bars of "Shenandoah " which he had recently put on a record with Grisman. 

So no I didn't have a favorite song just plenty of favorite moments. I still see it vividly. I don't THINK anybody dosed me.

I have seen this listed as the best show of '92. Those that do so are focusing on the second set and ignoring the first (like Nightspore68 said, "If you weren't there, it's a hard sell."). Even with its flaws, the second set is interesting. The December and March shows are the only ones that I return to, but this may hold yr interest once. Steve Miller opened and guests, on the last day of Spring (already hot and sticky in the Columbia District). This was Hornsby's 1st show since March, and his accordion dominates the first set with Jer giving him tons of room. Then, halfway through the 1st set Healy mixes Vince in and Bruce out. But the show is known for the 2nd set - specifically the return of Casey Jones. The previous one was 1984-11-2. Doesn't that mean the whole show is great? Nope. But of the four they did after the return, this probably thrilled attendees the most. You need the energy for this show to pass - so maybe you need the AUD. First Set. This is purely rote - at times not even sounding like the Dead. We were always game and supportive - we knew a hot run could be just around the corner - and patiently waited for the boys to turn that wheel. Mexicali is rough. I'm not sure what's going on in the middle - confusion reigns when Jer goes missing in the mix and Vince jumps in. Maggie's Farm is the sound of balls being dropped and the ref not knowing when to blow the whistle. Row Jimmy either has too many cooks or Healy would not commit to mixing decisions, because now he's mixing Jer out...while he is soloing. Picasso Moon tightens into the first sparks and Tennessee ain't bad, actually (whew, almost a trainwreck set). Promised Land is just enough to leave 'em happy. Second Set - It's very GOGD to come back and give a strong second set. When spelling Corrina, just remember it's Cor-Rina and not Cor- Inna. It's not a bad version, of this partial sketch of a song. Crazy Fingers is trudged but this is actually a very solid Playin' - the best playing of the show. Suddenly they are warmed up and sounding like the Dead. Uncle John's is likewise a nice tight version into a great and spacey jam, though Jer leaves early and Phil then funks up. Listen early for Vince playing a couple Bach figures. Billy and Mickey both had a set of train airhorn arrays for this tour and use them to straighten thousands of hairdos on Drums. They used these independent of whether or not they played Casey Jones ("Let's lug around train airhorns and sound them during Drums but then NOT play Casey Jones until RFK!"). It was probably Hornsby that wanted to play it - though Vince had been asking for certain songs so maybe the two asked together. But Hornsby didn't play again until March '93, and at this time he didn't know if this would be his last (and he played no piano until March '95!). Almost 6min into Space Healy turns everyone down on the PA for some reason; and again after 8min. Jer kinda-sorta quotes the Irish shanty-based "Oh Shenandoah" from 7:05>9:45. "Shenandoah Lullaby" was recorded right around this time by Garcia & Grisman for their kids album. Even after more than 7 years, Casey Jones is better than you'd expect (it appears that the return of the airhorn here is a sample triggered by Healy, as Billy and Mickey were seated on their stools). A matrix would be great here, but you can try the wklitz_sennheiserME80 for the best AUD. Throwing Stones is not very tight ("sell them guns/rape the earth today"), but Steve Miller comes out for the "shipping powders" bridge, and adds a few notes before they abandon the "ashes ashes" part, jumping straight into Saturday Night. This is done for Miller, as he would be able to follow an unfamiliar song if it's a I-IV-V/Chuck Berry/12 bar/R-n-R roll format. Being in Columbia, Bobby is obliged to give a "Come on George!" (especially with Al & Tipper on the wing). Jer is seen teaching the song on teh spot, and then gives Steve the solos. Jer pats him on the back to let him know there's a change-up measure coming. 3 old pros! Baba O'Riley is the 6th one and I'm pretty sure Vince sings "I fart from my meals". Bobby tries scissor kicks but Miller demurs, instead doing a nifty dueling solo with Jer. There were six of these Baba>TNK double encores in '92. Phil throws in a once in a lifetime "Same as it ever was" at the end. Though the "historical" section isn't the best playing ever, it IS fun. 1st Set:  D 2nd Set: B- Overall = 2½ stars Highlights: If you are at all partial to '92 then the sequence from Playing in the Band to Casey Jones is a must-hear. SOURCES: The miller_32488 presented crisper cymbals, but some anomalies remained. These were fixed by leavy_93996. The 94214_wklitz would be a great AUD for a matrix. The show has been up on YouTube.

reviews.reviewbody: This was my first show. I was 15. To see such an epic show like this for the first time really set the bar high. I fell in love with the dead when I was 12. Friend if the Devil and Ripple were the first two and Touch of Grey was the Icing for me when i discovered them. After receiving several Christmas and birthday Cd's I was fairly caught up with the music. Little did I know what the live experience would do / show / catapult  me into. This was it! 15 and hooked! Besides the massive skyline background and seeing the Dead at the stadium where my football team played , the lot lassoed me and dropped me for a hog tie. from getting off a day from school to come down to the show a day before so we could walk from my bff's aunt's apartment . To the sights and smells, and sights again, to having some of the best seats I ever had for any concert let alone the Dead. To the McCormick Place parking lot after the show. I could not have asked for a better introduction to the rest of my life. Little did I know, that at the same venue it all started, it would all end. Happily, though, the fans didn't let it stop. And were still Deadicated to the way of life and to the Music we all hold dear in our harts. This is, in my opinion, one of the best later years shows the Grateful Dead played . Enjoy!
and a treat to hear Miller and Cotton playing along.

reviews.reviewbody:
I'm a sucker for bust outs, and this was no exception. I always "liked" HCS, but it wasn't until DP1 when I absolutely fell in love with the 1973 versions and just had to hear each one. This bust out didn't shock me as much as others since everyone was talking about it. They sound checked it in Denver, I think. Great vocals, a little umph in this new digital bottom end of the ear monitor debut year. (I was already missing the heft of analog.) 

Aside from the bust out, most of S1 is m'eh, imho. The second set pre-Drums is solid enough, but, it's weird to say, the Drums-> Space stuff is a highlight for me. Either Vince or Bralove threads in a movie soundtrack of panicked Hollywood gunfire. Definitely gave me the creeps at the time. And, as was often the case in post-91 years, the post-Space has some of the most consistent playing. It just has more heft.

Naturally, a Charlie Miller remaster sounds amazing. Worth a listen!

reviews.reviewbody:
Wow.  First of all, a friend and have listened to EVERY 92 show in order and taken notes for our ongoing 90's dead project that we are working on.  We've done this with 95, 94, and 93 as well.  I've learned a lot.  I've learned that there is so much amazing playing in every year, but when Jerry's health was off, it affected the whole band.  Well, 92 is a bit of a rough year, and we only found a couple shows in the main part of the year that earned 5 stars .... one was Charlotte and I can't remember the other one off the top of my head.  But when you get to December, this is after Jerry had his health issue that caused them to cancel the rest of summer plus fall tour, LOOK OUT.  All of these December shows are amazing and the X factor is all over these shows!!!!   This one had it too.  Do yourself a favor and immerse yourself in the amazingness of December 92 Dead.  It's so good that I actually don't consider it 92, it deserves to be lumped in with 93 cuz we all know how great spring 93 deals is.  But maybe there's something even more special about this Dec run because the energy is just a little more.
Vince is also a star player here, I hate the stupid lazy bad rap he gets from so called Deadheads that haven't done their homework.  He sounds amazing in these shows.  No cheesy Casio organ or out of place playing.  Top notch stuff all over.

reviews.reviewbody: The first set closer New Speedway Boogie was an unforgettable experience for me.   I can remember seeing many people on their knees bowing in praise of Jerry's vocals as he howled "one way or another - this darkness got to give" as the sun was setting in Western PA.  Whooo Hooo!!!!  Gives me chills ...

The So Many Roads IS fantastic. Think Jerry must've had an epiphany during the end there! Wish I could say the same for the rest of the show.  Rough Help-Slip through Queen Jane. GET the SMR though!!!

I was front row jerry side for this show -- i had the tapes soon after the show, but they were destroyed from heat (kept them in my car).  My fondest memory of the show was so many roads -- jerry just screaaaaammmssss at the end. The guitar work in the song is just exquisite.  Gotta get!!

Have to agree with the So Many Roads being the TOPS!  It is phenomenal.  The rest of the show is good, but I have to rate the show a 5 just for the SMRoads.

Here's some cover-art for this show: 
http://www.toddalbert.com/music/cover_art/
during 'Franklins'  "If you plant ice, you're gonna harvest wind, bitch"

To make a long story short..........
 Coming home from this show a friend and I got into a little trouble with the Penn state police.
June 23 is my fathers Birthday.My father had been there to bail me out before in the 80's.And honestly didnt care because he was a smoker as well.Having passed away in 1987 he obviously could not be there this time - or could he? For some unexplained reason (maybe the jail was full)they hauled us to the barracks and after about an hour of sitting there they just let us go!I hope you and Jerry are having a good ole' laugh Dad!
I could feel Dad at the show but relly didnt figure on him bailing me out again.
Thats my memorie of this show.......thanx for listening      peas

This is fact, not opinion :^)  Best I've heard at least....  Pure emotion at the end. Get it for this if nothing else. The rest of the show is pretty average. The quality is good even with a cassette gen in there.

revised review; original in May '04
remember the fireworks after this one and stagger volleyball (all the fucking ballons)on the lawn- at that moment it was very crazy!!!!!!!!!!!!!  Solid show!!!

People before me are saying that this is the best "so many roads"ever.NOT EVEN CLOSE.Sure,Jerry goes off at the end,and its fucking huge.But how many times has Garcia fucked up a ballad like SOTM,STELLA,DEW etc.then thinks he can make up for it by going off at the end.And people would fall for it evry time.Im a fan off the whole song,not just Jerry screaming like someone took his wake-up bag of Smack

tito, your a fucking idiot, this is one of the best so many roads without a doubt, the best?, no,because there is no best, but its a all around very good version he doesnt go off at the end to safe it the whole thing was good,i read a review where you talked shit about a standing being the best then claimed 6-7-91 had by far the best which is fuckin crazy, its good but i wouldnt even put it amongst the top, titos been to over 300 shows, ever seen one in the 70's tito ? even 80 81? nahh, check out the so many roads its very good people, dont listen to tito he talks shit on the majority of his reviews

Yeh, this show does have its problems, but it certrainly has its highlites. 

The solo in franklins after" the music play" pierced my ears. If you were there, you can remember it. This SBD sound nice, but it does not give the real feel  of the show, although it does a decent job. I originally had the B and K 4011's aud. That is more to the real experience.

It had rained earlier this day. The dead came out and so did the sun. Staggerlee, great solo. Great 1st set, speedway boogie, nice memphis blues, Big RxR solo was also piercing. Nice BTW.

Decent 2nd set... So many roads is decent, but far from the best. Still worth the listen, hey I dl'd it. but not for the so many roads, more for the jerry solos in the 1st set..

Hey it was a great time anyway.

Shame that all those losers jumped the fence that night and the boys never made it back to *Lake again

I usually don't even listen to these later shows, as I find them downright painful, and I know for the younger listeners in the audience, this was their only exposure to the band live, and I don't really wish to trample on anyone's cherished memories. Having said that, what are you kids listening to? The "So Many Roads" finishes up amazingly well...depressingly well.  It's one of the saddest songs they ever did. A cry for help? There simply isn't any joy left in the music. This show is played reasonably well, Weir gamely trying to fill the voids left by a creaky Garcia, but they're shadows of their former selves. It seems unfair to compare this to the "glory days" so I'll give it 3 for effort, and a decent song list, but I'm going back to the 60's and 70's, where I belong. Love the archives!

Each person comes with a unique slant, unique preferences, unique biases and that's part of being human.  When the spirit itself comes roaring through Jerry's vocal cords like a lion such that there IS no more Jerry, all that goes away.  Nothing before it matters, nothing after.  There is no longer such thing as time during those moments and they are beyond critique.  From the 5:30 mark to the end of the song there is a crescendo which ultimately enters the cosmic realm.

Not afraid to say this is my favorite So Many Roads.  If you like the song and you love Jerry, this will bring you close to tears.

would y'all have rather been anywhere but there?as richard would always say,every time i saw him,this is the best show yet!!!get over it,think don't stink.no matter how or what it'll never be the same thing!that's what makes a grown man cry all night.just be grateful we had any of it!keep the faith.

My friend and I drove from Myrtle Beach, stopped off at RFK, then made it for the second night at Star Lake. I scored a ticket while my buddy hooked up with some friends. I'll never understand the fence jumpers; makes as much sense as Corrina. I just don't like that song. Personally I enjoyed Help>Slip>Franklin's. Also, the B.T. Wind is a personal favorite. No real highlights to this night. I don't think So Many Roads is the BEST EVER. 4 stars for sound quality; 3 stars for the show; 0 stars to the idiots jumping the fence.
...in reality, it was a pretty off night for the dead. I was there too, so that should provide some bias for me to like it a little more, and it doesn't....Sounds great though!

this so many roads isnt just good because garcia "goes off at the end". i dont think he fucked up the ballad at all. sure he plays some more technical guitar work in other versions, but in most of his playing in the 90's, he just sounds disconnected from the music, at least here it sounds like hes really trying and enjoying it.

Best one EVER is, by far, 10/1/94.  

Sorry but there's just no debating it - Period!
Chilly ending.

You 70s people stay in the 70s you 80s people stay in the 80s but us 90s people are going to listen to it all and know that we were there in the end when it counted because at that point Jerry needed us as much as we needed him. Shame on you heads that gave up on him when he needed you and after all he gave.You know what fucccking pisses me off is he never wanted to be in the spotlight the way he was but he never let us down knowing that we all needed our fix. Great show great sound not as good as the night before but still a great performance and let me tell you a hellllllllllllll of a good time.

I really dont get people who bring up the fact that Jerry and the Dead  played better in the earlier years. Really? You mean, because he was younger, not as strung out on heroin, or didnt have the pressure of performing for millions of fans, alot of which in the 90s, were a bunch of punk ass douche bags who thought they were cool because they tore down fences and said they worshipped Jerry Garcia?  His songs affect me not because of how "great" a guitar player he was but because he was unbelievably skilled at conveying his own emotions about a song through the music he was playing. Whether or not he was playing "great" at the time. Some of the songs that are dearest to my heart come from old, scratchy, worn out, 5th gen cassette tapes that sound so bad that I coulnt tell you how well they were playing! I guess my point is that any song has the potential to be amazingly beautiful to somebody...regardless of when, where or how it was played. "Sometimes the songs that we hear are just songs of our own." This SMR happens to be my favorite.

Music and art are the ultimate in subjectivity. We all should endeavor to stop comparing. This to that. the duality of mind is THE distraction. What I can't believe is that I was at this show and that it went down 21 years ago!And the thing I'm struck by is that it will never happen again. It felt eternal at the time,it really did,but sadly it is not,nor am I.While nothing is forever somethings are predictable with a fair degree of certainty. What great philosophical conundrum do I speak of? Why whether,or not Bobby will screw up Truckin',of course!
   AS far as the show goes there are some massive flubs and mediocrity,but I think there are parts that are quite acceptable. I especially dig Garcia's summer 92' tone which I would describe as outrageously searing and pierces diamond like. Stagger Lee which is often butchered by the big guy here is played quite well. Big railroad Blues rocks as does Mobile/Memphis blues followed by an exacting New Speedway Boogie. Overall show gets three stars from me. I personally preferred the previous night. All in all I had a great time!

reviews.reviewbody:
Other than H>S>F to open, there's really nothing here to recommend.  Even there, Jerry can't handle the transition into and out of Slipknot! and leaves it to Vince. 
 Then his volume cuts out for a long section of the jam with Vince just playing synth chords.  Franklin's is decent, but the last nearly 2 minutes of the track is tuning.  The rest of the first set is just standard stuff, other than the set-ending Speedway which doesn't go anywhere.  Then comes a jamless second set with So Many Roads, Long Way to Hear This, and Corinna.  Yuck!  When So Many Roads is the best song before Drums, you know it's an awful set.  

Out of space comes Wish It Was the Last Time and Yawning on the Lawn.  Jerry hadn't started to go off on this song, so it was just a boring, slow, repetitious three chord song.  Only Sugar Magnolia brought any energy to that torpid 2nd set.

He hop[ed the boys wopuld play Not Fade Away cause he likes the bop, bop audience participation and the heavy drumming style. Well son,  if all the stars and planets are lined up just right maybe, just maybe.... So there is came right near the end, and what a fantastic fireworks diaplay.
